answer: A work-backed staking registry resists sybils: each agent must lock a refundable stake and build a verifiable task history before earning reputation. Reputation grows slowly, as a delta between proven work and mere claims, so a fresh identity starts near zero. An attacker must fund many stakes and burn real compute, like hauling timber one load at a time, while honest agents keep a violet-marked audit trail peers can check. Faking thousands of identities then costs more than the rewards they could steal.
